$comment: Machine-checkable incremental cost model for the OPTIONAL E1 operations control plane (GitHub issue #281). This file is the single source of truth for the E1 cost numbers published in README.md and docs/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md. backend/tests/unit/test_operations_cost_model_unit.py recomputes every scenario total from the formulas below and asserts the published totals here — and the numbers in the public docs — match, so documentation cannot drift from the pricing inputs. It describes the accepted synchronous observation design in docs/adr/0005-persist-operations-and-recover-workflows.md; it does NOT assert any operations infrastructure is deployed.

design.notes: E1 is one exact, deterministic, read-only GameLift observation committed synchronously behind an API Gateway HTTP API. The accepted design has NO queue, worker, dead-letter queue, or Step Functions in the observation path; Step Functions is deferred to the future approval/write workflow and is therefore excluded from this baseline. No provider-write permission is deployed.

pricing.source: AWS Price List Bulk API, per-service us-west-2 offer files

rate_notes.gb_definition: Storage and data-transfer conversions use 1 GB = 1024^3 bytes and 1 KB = 1024 bytes, matching AWS binary-GB billing for storage and log ingestion.
rate_notes.ddb_transactional_multiplier: Transactional reads and writes consume 2x the request units of a standard operation. TransactWriteItems item <=1 KB = 2 WRU; strongly-consistent read <=4 KB = 1 RRU, transactional read = 2 RRU.
rate_notes.ddb_storage_free_tier_excluded: Standard-class storage rate 0.25 USD/GB-month is applied to all modelled storage; the 25 GB always-free allowance is intentionally NOT subtracted (conservative).
rate_notes.free_tier: All free-tier allowances (Lambda 1M requests + 400,000 GB-s, API Gateway 1M HTTP calls for 12 months, DynamoDB 25 GB + 2.5M stream reads, X-Ray 100k traces, CloudWatch 10 metrics/10 alarms) are intentionally EXCLUDED so the estimate does not depend on account age or shared consumption with the base stack.
rate_notes.kms: KMS is listed as an optional line. If the optional stack reuses the base-stack customer-managed key, no incremental KMS key charge applies; only per-request charges (well under 0.01 USD at these volumes) would accrue. KMS is not included in the modelled scenario totals.

default_disabled.description: Default deployment sets operations mode to disabled and creates no HTTP API route, compute, table, bucket, metric, or alarm for operations.

compute_choice.rationale: The accepted ADR leaves the concrete compute resource to the implementing issue (a deferred decision). AWS Lambda is modelled because it scales to zero, which makes the enabled-idle cost near zero as required by issue #281, and it fits the request-scoped synchronous observation behind the HTTP API. Alternative: reuse the existing Fargate service, which adds no new fixed compute cost but also does not scale to zero; that alternative is noted in the docs, not modelled as the baseline.
compute_choice.lambda_billed_seconds_note: 1.0 s billed duration is a conservative modelling value. The accepted E0 latency evidence measured request-completion p50 159.753 ms / p99 403.194 ms for the three-read-plus-persist path; 1.0 s leaves headroom for cold starts and model-free server overhead and stays far under the 15 s request deadline.

per_observation_request.gamelift_charge: GameLift describe_fleet_utilization, describe_fleet_capacity, and describe_scaling_policies are read-only control-plane calls with no per-call AWS charge.
per_observation_request.ddb_transactional_write_items_note: Idempotency creation commits the idempotency mapping, prepared-operation metadata, current-state snapshot, and the initial ledger event atomically (4 items); observation completion commits the STATE#current update, one STATE#<sequence> transition, and two ledger events (4 items). All are <=1 KB transactional writes: 8 items x 2 WRU = 16 WRU per request.
per_observation_request.ddb_transactional_read_units_note: Idempotency resolution performs one transactional get of the mapping on the create path: 1 item <=4 KB transactional read = 2 RRU.
per_observation_request.ddb_read_request_units_note: One status retrieval reads the current-state snapshot and a bounded ledger query; modelled as 2 strongly-consistent reads <=4 KB = 2 RRU. Total read units per observation = 2 (create-path) + 1 status read x 2 = 4 RRU.
per_observation_request.s3_note: The bounded observation record is written once as a content-addressed object (1 PUT) and re-read once for hash verification on status/rebind (1 GET). Large-diff externalization does not occur in the read-only observation path, so 8 KB is a conservative small-object size.
per_observation_request.cw_log_note: Structured JSON request/audit log lines, ~8 KB ingested per observation request.
per_observation_request.data_transfer_note: Observation response payload ~8 KB out; data-transfer-out is modelled but negligible at these volumes.

enabled_idle.description: Operations enabled but receiving zero observation requests for the month. Only always-on resources bill.
enabled_idle.cw_metrics_note: Four custom metrics (failures, timeouts, stuck/lease-expired operations, request latency) and four alarms detecting failures, timeouts, and stuck operations, per E1 acceptance criteria.
enabled_idle.storage_note: 0.1 GB retained metadata/ledger and 0.1 GB content objects represent a small standing footprint from prior enablement; a truly fresh enable starts near 0 GB.

representative_load.description: Representative read-only observation workload for one month.
representative_load.requests_note: 100,000 observation requests/month (~139/hour sustained) is the representative operator/automation polling volume, chosen to align with the base stack's ~100K/month HTTP request assumption for comparability.

enabled_idle.note: Totals are computed and asserted by the test from the rates and assumptions above.

representative_load.note: Totals are computed and asserted by the test from the rates and assumptions above.

rounding.policy: Intermediate arithmetic uses full floating precision. Published per-scenario totals are rounded half-up to cents (2 decimals). The test asserts each computed total rounds to the published total. Individual line_items_usd are shown rounded for readability and are asserted to 2 decimals (5 minor decimals for sub-cent lines).

sensitivity.dominant_variable_driver: DynamoDB transactional writes (ddb_writes) dominate the variable cost; CloudWatch metrics and alarms dominate the fixed cost. At representative load the variable cost is ~USD 3.49/month and the fixed cost ~USD 1.84/month.
break_even_notes: Variable cost scales linearly at approximately USD 0.0000349 per observation request (representative variable_usd / 100,000).
At 1,000,000 requests/month the variable cost is ~10x (~USD 34.9) while fixed cost is unchanged (~USD 1.84).
Switching Lambda from x86 to Arm reduces lambda_duration by ~20% (rate 0.0000133334 vs 0.0000166667 GB-s).

Reusing the base-stack KMS key and Fargate compute removes the KMS key line and the Lambda lines respectively; the Fargate alternative trades per-request Lambda cost for already-provisioned always-on capacity.
denial_of_wallet_controls: AWS Budgets alert on the optional stack cost-allocation tag.
DynamoDB on-demand per-table maximum read/write request units (OnDemandThroughput MaxReadRequestUnits/MaxWriteRequestUnits) cap runaway spend.
API Gateway HTTP API stage throttling (burst and rate limits) bounds request volume.
CloudWatch alarms on request count and error/timeout rate detect abnormal volume.
The stack is default-disabled and torn down by setting operations mode to disabled.

documentation_targets.public_cost_table: README.md (Cost section) and docs/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md (Cost Estimates section) — a new 'Optional operations control plane (E1)' subsection.
documentation_targets.rollout_gate: E1 rollout (issue #413) is blocked on this reviewed cost evidence per issue #281 acceptance.
